newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Rampant dollar fuels Euro share surge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Rampant dollar fuels Euro share surge.

text.p: The dollar's strength ignited Europe's major bourses on Wednesday with London and Paris ending at record levels and Germany coming within a whisker of a closing peak.

The dollar stormed to its highest level in more than 2-1/2 years against the German mark when it touched 1.6455 helping to lift German shares a hefty 1.75 percent. French and British shares also surged 1.35 and 0.56 percent respectively.
"It's the strong dollar that is underpinning everything today and no-one can afford to be out of the market," said one German share trader.
The German bourse particularly benefited from the stonger dollar because of the many large exporting companies listed.
The dollar also propelled French stocks higher in heavy volume and the blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 32.58 points, at a closing high of 2,442.46, having touched 2,450.34 points.
"The dollar's fabulous," one French share trader said. "The money just keeps flowing in."

The dollar hit a high of 5.5453 francs on Wednesday, bringing its gains against the French currency to 10 percent over two months. Economists expect a stronger dollar to spur French exports and investment.
London's FTSE 100 also closed at a record high as both share and bond investors hoped British interest rates would not be raised in the near-term.
A weak start on Wall Street pushed prices off their best level late in the session but dealers expect the FTSE to set new highs in the coming weeks provided the Dow remains steady.
The FTSE 100 also set an intraday trading high of 4,227.5 before closing at 4,219.1, up 23.6 points on the day, surpassing the previous record closing high of 4,207.7, set on January 17.
"The Dow took a bit of steam out of the market but people are still pretty confident," one senior dealer said. "I suspect we will be setting more new highs in the coming weeks."

The Dow plunged over 70 points in the opening minutes of trade after U.S. brokers cut earnings estimates for IBM. But U.S. blue chips clawed back some of the losses to stand around 60 points lower by the London close at 6824.63.

Earlier, European markets rose on the back of the overnight testimony to the U.S. Senate of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan in which he gave markets no cause for alarm over the course of the U.S. economy.
Only last month he wiped billions off share values by warning of "irrational exuberance".

In currencies, the dollar stormed to its highest level in more than 2-1/2 years against the German mark and almost four years against the yen as American, European and Japanese authorities appeared to give its recent rally a green light.

The dollar succumbed to some mild profit-taking later in the day as U.S. stocks and bonds also pared some of their recent gains. Bundesbank member Ernst Welteke also helped keep a lid on it as he cautioned about the pace of recent mark depreciation.
However, analysts remained bullish on the dollar outlook against European currencies in particular.

"There's an underlying feeling that no one in power is unhappy with the extent of the dollar's rise, although the pace may be seen as a little excessive," said Adrian Schmidt, economist at Chase Investment Bank.
The dollar set a 47-month high at 119.20 yen early in the session and a 32-month high at 1.4360 Swiss francs.
The dollar's rise hurt gold prices, which slipped under $350.00 per ounce for the first time since mid September 1993, leaving market analysts predicting a bumpy ride ahead for the precious metal.
The dollar's strength makes dollar-priced commodities like gold unattractively expensive for buyers in marks or yens.
CURRENCIES AT 1715 GMT
The dollar stood at 118.70 yen and 1.6380 marks from Tuesday's late European levels of 117.78 and 1.6240.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 23.6 points higher at 4,219.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 32.58 at 2,442.46.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 51.96 at 3,028.67.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1715 GMT
Gold closed at $350.15 after falling to $349.70 in the morning from a $353.65 close in London on Tuesday.
